prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In a top-down view onto a carpeted indoor floor, a person lies curled on their left side across the upper-left and middle of the frame (roughly 1.0 to 1.8 m below the standing camera wearer), while a medium-sized dog lies on the floor to the lower-right (roughly 0.8 to 1.5 m away, and 0.2 to 0.6 m in front of the lying person until moving against their legs in frames 4–5). In frames 1–3, the camera wearer's extended hands enter from the bottom edge at 0.3 to 0.7 m depth—putting the dog well within the wearer's arm's reach while the lying person curls with hands near their own head—and across frames 1–5 the camera wearer steps back or stands upright so both subjects retreat farther below and the upper-right wall base becomes visible at over 2 m. While the lying person's head stays at the lower-left edge facing downward and slightly right away from the camera, the dog initially faces lower-left and then turns its raised head upward to look directly toward the camera wearer in frames 4 and 5, partially occluding the person's knees. The depth map clearly separates the foreground height of the wearer's reaching forearms, the raised elevation of the lying person's hip and shoulder, and the dog's elevated head from the flat dark-shirted and dark-furred textures that blend together in RGB, though it is unreliable where the floor gradient shifts non-uniformly across frames and where the dog's head merges smoothly into the person's legs in frames 4–5.
descriptions.segmentation: Across the five frames on the carpeted floor, the instance segmentation outlines the lying person in the upper-left (1.0 to 1.8 m from the wearer, facing down and right away from the lens) and the dog roughly 0.2 to 0.6 m to the lower-right (0.8 to 1.5 m from the wearer), along with the camera wearer's foreground left arm reaching from the bottom edge in frames 1–3 to touch the dog within 0.5–0.8 m arm's reach. As the camera viewpoint retreats and tilts slightly upward from frame 1 to frame 5, the wearer's arms withdraw out of the bottom of the frame (where one of the wearer's feet briefly appears at the bottom-left in frame 3), and the dog shifts from facing lower-left to sitting up and looking directly at the camera wearer while pressing against and partially occluding the lying person's thighs. The segmentation masks make the sharp outer silhouettes of the dark-clothed person, the black-and-white dog, and the wearer's reaching arm immediately distinct against the shadowed carpet in frames 1, 2, and 5 despite low RGB contrast. However, the map is highly unreliable in class labels and temporal consistency: it mislabels the dog as a person in frame 1, splits the lying person into two masks while leaving their black shirt unsegmented in frame 2, hallucinates a giant 'sandwich' mask over the carpet in frame 3 while missing both subjects, and merges the person and dog into a single 'cat' mask in frame 4 and a single 'person' mask in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: On the black background, the pose map attempts to track skeletal keypoints within the indoor floor scene containing the lying person on the left (1.0 to 1.8 m below the camera wearer, curled on their side facing down-right away from the camera) and the dog 0.2 to 0.6 m to their lower-right (0.8 to 1.5 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach during frames 1–3). Across the sequence, the camera wearer's hands reach into the lower foreground in frames 1–3 and then retract out of view in frames 4–5 as the viewpoint pulls back and the dog turns its head upward toward the camera in front of the person's legs. When detections occur in frames 2 and 5, the yellow body lines indicate the horizontal, bent-knee orientation of a figure lying across the floor that can be hard to parse from the dark clothing in RGB alone. However, the pose map is severely unreliable throughout: it completely misses all bodies and the camera wearer's foreground magenta hand skeletons in frames 1, 3, and 4, erroneously fits a human body skeleton onto the dog's torso and head in frame 2, and collapses the lying person's upper torso and head into tangled, misplaced keypoints in frame 5 where the dog's head occludes their legs.
